sentences.text:
The short grievance of the petitioners is that the lands of the petitioners have been acquired by the State under the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Act, 1966 (for short, 'KIAD Act') as regards which the award has been passed under the Land Acquisition Act 1894 and not under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, the 'Act of 2013').
3.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The submission of Sri.Harshavardhan R.Malipatil, learned counsel for the petitioners is that the very notification issued under sub-section (1) of Section 28 of the KIAD Act had categorically indicated that any developments which were made to the property subject matter of the proposed acquisition would not be taken into consideration for the purpose of - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6937 awardal of compensation under the Act of 2013 and as such, on that basis,
he submits that insofar as the lands acquired are concerned, compensation is required to be paid under the Act of 2013.
The award could not have been passed under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and as such, the relief sought for are required to be granted.

Sri A.M.Nagral, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1-SLAO KIADB would submit that what is excluded under the said notification is the improvement made post the notification and that exclusion will not come to the benefit of the petitioners insofar as claiming compensation as regards the land under the Act of 2013 and as such, he submits that Act of 2013 would not be applicable for the purpose of calculation of compensation in respect to the lands acquired.
5. Sri
.Sudhir Singh R. Vijapur, learned counsel for respondent No.3 would submit that respondent No.3 - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6937 has nothing to do with the matter.
Since with regard to compensation payable, the land has been allotted to respondent No.3 free of cost.

6. Heard Sri.Harshavardhan R.Malipatil, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri.A.M.Nagral,
learned counsel for the respondent No.1-SLAO KIADB and Sri. Sudhirsingh R.Vijapur, learned DSGI for respondent No.3 and perused the papers.
7.

Though a very novel argument has been addressed by Sri.A.M.Nagral, learned counsel for respondent No.1- SLAO KIADB, I am unable to accept the same when the notification itself indicates that development put up on the land will be excluded for the purpose of consideration while passing an award and that consideration is to be made under the Act of 2013, the same would necessarily imply that the compensation as regards the lands and the improvements already made prior to the notification - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6937 being issued would be done in terms of the Act of 2013.
Admittedly, the notification in these matters has been issued on 07.11.2017, much after the 2013 Act came into force on 01.01.2014.
It is but required that compensation is required to be paid as regards the lands acquired post the Act of 2013, coming into force under the Act of 2013.

8. As regards the submission of Sri.Sudhirsingh R.Vijapur, learned DSGI for respondent No.3, the same is not subject matter, as the lis in the present matter is between the State and respondent No.3 as regards which this Court cannot express any opinion.

9. Hence, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Writ petitions are allowed.
ii.
The reliefs sought for are moulded.

13 - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6937 to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation, Resettlement Act, 2013 after giving due deduction to the earlier award passed under Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

The short grievance of the petitioners is that the lands of the petitioners have been acquired by the State under the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Act, 1966 (for short, 'KIAD Act') as regards which the award has been passed under the Land Acquisition Act 1894 and not under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, the 'Act of 2013').
3.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The award could not have been passed under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and as such, the relief sought for are required to be granted.
Though a very novel argument has been addressed by Sri.A.M.Nagral, learned counsel for respondent No.1- SLAO KIADB, I am unable to accept the same when the notification itself indicates that development put up on the land will be excluded for the purpose of consideration while passing an award and that consideration is to be made under the Act of 2013, the same would necessarily imply that the compensation as regards the lands and the improvements already made prior to the notification - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6937 being issued would be done in terms of the Act of 2013.
It is but required that compensation is required to be paid as regards the lands acquired post the Act of 2013, coming into force under the Act of 2013.
8. As regards the submission of Sri.Sudhirsingh R.Vijapur, learned DSGI for respondent No.3, the same is not subject matter, as the lis in the present matter is between the State and respondent No.3 as regards which this Court cannot express any opinion.
